title: Computer use inside the agent's own sandbox desktop (consent tiers only if user-desktop control is ever unparked)
summary: Add a computer tool whose Model-proposed actions (screenshot plus accessibility tree, click, type, scroll) are executed by a guest agent on a desktop inside the item 3 sandbox VM, with receipts for every action. Adopt the 'typed connectors first, then browser, then screen' hierarchy now as policy; build Claude-style per-app consent tiers and an Endpoint Plane executor only if the owner later allows control of user machines.
whyItMatters: 'Controls a computer, acts like a PC' is part of the stated vision, and desktop computer use is a table-stakes feature in 8 of 12 sources. Doing it in the agent's own VM delivers the capability while respecting the owner's decision not to drive users' own desktops and the rule that the Model proposes and the executor acts.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Manus (accessibility-first engine: UI Automation tree with short handles, element-targeted actions, synthesized input only as fallback, strict window-identity ladder) plus Claude (per-app consent tiers, deny list, machine lock, restoration at turn end)
others: Hermes (any-model computer use via a cua-driver MCP with numbered elements)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 8 of 12 sources (table-stakes); consent tiers are a differentiator (2 of 12)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: get_app_state returns {a11y tree with handles, optional screenshot with capture id}; act{handle | coords+capture_id}; targets resolve through a window-identity ladder and ambiguous targets are refused; provider-native computer-use schemas map onto the same engine. Consent: request_access{app} gives a tier from the app category (view-only browsers, click-only terminals, full otherwise), enforced on every action against the frontmost app, with a deny list, a global lock and restoration of windows and clipboard at turn end.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: There is no computer-use tool anywhere in Model Plane. OS-level desktop control was parked by the owner (recorded in the chat parity audit). The Endpoint Plane is a native Rust remote-desktop host with screen capture, input injection and a consent prompt, but no agent tool targets it. Verevon's typed-actions-first policy already matches Claude's connectors-then-browser-then-screen hierarchy in spirit, but it is not written as a rule the model sees.

approachOriginal: Phase 1 (after item 3): an Xfce or Wayland desktop in the VM image; execution-core exposes a computer tool (screenshot, AT-SPI accessibility tree, xdotool or ydotool input); the guest agent executes and returns structured receipts reusing Quarry's receipt and tri-state verification model (step_receipts.rs); every action passes capability policy and the Model never executes. Write the tool-hierarchy rule into the system prompt and capability policy now. Phase 2, only if the owner unparks user-desktop control: the Endpoint Plane agent as executor with per-app consent tiers, deny list and machine lock.
planeOwner: Model Plane (execution-core computer tool, guest agent); Endpoint Plane only for phase 2
risks: Pixel-agent reliability, prompt injection from on-screen content, vision-token cost, and the owner's parked decision on user-machine control; consent tiers add little value until phase 2.

verevon.exactGap: No computer or desktop tool exists in Model Plane: the Do-mode catalogue offers only browser.observe/browser.act (Quarry browser runs; the act schema refuses coordinates, URLs and raw CDP) and code_interpreter, the execution substrate is a one-shot bubblewrap child (sandbox.rs capability profile: ephemeral, bounded_oneshot, no durable computer), the sandbox-manager image carries no desktop packages and 'desktop' is rejected as a browser-broker grant mode. The Endpoint Plane Verevon Agent is a Windows-only RustDesk-protocol host (cfg(windows) capture and input, native consent dialog) that no Model Plane tool targets, and OS-level desktop control is recorded as parked by the owner. The only shipped analogue is browser-level: Quarry's AgentAction with snapshot-scoped ClickRef/TypeRef refs and generation checks, a CDP accessibility projection, and append-only step receipts.

verevon.constraints: Model proposes, executor acts: a desktop executor inside a sandbox VM is not Quarry, so the browser rule does not transfer by itself; keep Model Plane as proposer, run the guest agent under a lease bound to one Space and a Control-signed capability decision, and route every action through capability_policy (trusted_capability_id fails closed for any unmapped tool id, so a new cap id is needed). The browser tool deliberately refuses coordinates; a desktop tool with coords + capture_id reopens the pixel channel that surface closed, so it needs an ADR and per-action risk classes. Web access must stay on Quarry (ingestion executes or rejects, BrowserBroker grants, egress policy); a desktop browser inside the VM must not become a second, ungoverned browser path. ZDR must propagate to screenshots and receipts (Quarry AgentActionRequest already carries ZdrMode), and Space access must never widen an owner-plane ACL. Driving the user's own desktop is parked by the owner, so phase 2 stays parked.

The existing Endpoint Plane agent cannot be reused inside a Linux VM (Windows-only), and Linux AT-SPI coverage of real GUI apps is unverified.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged. The S policy-rule piece is separable and cheap; nearly all XL cost sits in F-t3-009's VM backend and typed executor protocol, which this item must not double count.
verevon.verdictReason: The absent claim is correct, but the item reads as a standalone first-rank build when it is the capstone of F-t3-009 and F-t3-035 plus an ADR. Browser-level computer use (a11y refs, receipts, approvals) already ships in Quarry and should be the model, and the pixel-coordinate fallback conflicts with a deliberate current policy. Split out the S hierarchy rule.

title: Open the typed action registry to the agent: classify every action, admit reads first, mint per-run scoped tokens
summary: Verevon's single typed action registry shared by the UI and agents is the reference design, but only 8 actions are model-executable. Classify every action by model access (none, read, write-with-approval, write) and risk, admit read actions per owning plane through the capability gate, then writes under item 01's exact-effect approval, and mint per-run delegated tokens scoped to the thread and capability set.
whyItMatters: This is the core of the AI-first thesis: the user can say 'move this to my Space and notify the team' and the agent performs it with the same actions and guards as the UI. 4 of 12 sources expose their own product to the agent; Claude desktop and T3 Code show the pattern.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Claude desktop (built-in MCP servers for sessions, sidebar, settings and host actions; each Preferences key declares whether the model may read or change it; SRC) plus T3 Code (per-session scoped bearer credential stored only as a hash; SRC)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: A typed action registry shared by UI and agent; each action declares model access (none | read | write-with-approval | write) and risk; admitted actions become tools with honest annotations (readOnly, destructive, idempotent); a per-session scoped token limited to the thread and capability set is issued and stored only as a hash.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: The registry has 168 typed actions (chat/agents baseline v-chat-agents-ui-088; not recounted here), but the model-eligibility allowlist admits only 8: tickets.create, inbox.follow_conversation, inbox.set_csat_preference, inbox.review_ai_action, chat.save_thread_snapshot, chat.submit_feedback, org.mark_exported and org.acknowledge_deletion (SRC). There are no per-setting model-access classes and no session-scoped tool credentials recorded. Each admission needs owner-plane proof (contract, attestation, forged-call denial test), which is why the list is deliberately short.

approachOriginal: Frontend Plane action registry plus Model Plane capability gate. Add model-access and risk metadata to ActionDescriptor and a CI ratchet that follows the AI-first plan (M2: at least 10 eligible low-risk actions; M3: all eligible actions with explicit exemptions). Treat each admission as per-owner design work (owner contract, capability binding, health attestation, forged-call denial test). Keep security, billing and identity settings non-model-accessible. Writes use item 01's policy and exact-effect approval; the BFF gateway mints a per-run scoped delegated token bound to the thread and capability set.
planeOwner: Frontend Plane (registry, token minting at the BFF gateway) with the Model Plane capability gate and each owning plane
risks: Agents acting on account settings (keep security and identity settings out); admitting an action without owner proof ships a dead or unsafe tool (the repo has hit this before); delegated authority needs a Control decision.

alreadyPlanned.where: Verevon-ai-first-plan.md milestones M2 and M3 (lines 42-43, 92-102): at least 10 eligible actions by M2, all eligible actions by M3 with CI enforcement.

verevon.exactGap: ActionDescriptor already carries risk, requiresApproval and reversible, and a versioned, hashed catalog manifest with allowedActorTypes and an executionContract exists (types.ts:15-24, catalog-manifest.ts:32-70), but there is no read versus write model-access class, no human-only exempt marker and no CI ratchet; isModelExecutableAction admits 8 of 168 actions (model-eligibility.ts:126-140). A per-run, per-action signed authority already exists in Control (run-action-v1 and model-action-view-v1, bound to run id, thread id, subject, schema hash, payload digest and idempotency key), but runActionTarget accepts only tickets.create (run_action_decision.go:340-347) and the model-action view is a pinned single action, with a bespoke Model Plane adapter (ticket_tools.rs). The BFF mints per-audience per-user bearers (chat/shared.rs:187-260), not per-run tokens.
reuse: ActionDescriptor fields risk, requiresApproval and reversible, and buildActionCatalogManifest (deterministic hash, allowedActorTypes)
catalog-manifest.test.ts allowlist assertion as the seed of the CI ratchet
Control user-core RunActionDecision and ModelActionView signing, plus capability-core ControlModelActionViewVerifier
execution-core ticket_tools.rs as the pattern for an owner-action adapter (Control decision, then owner receipt)
Verevon-ai-first-plan.md three-tier model (model-eligible, approval-gated, human-only exempt) and scoreboard idea
verevon.constraints: Control resolves actor, org, Space, audience and privacy itself; the caller supplies only identifiers and commitments (model_action_decision.go:13-24), so scoped authority must be minted by Control user-core, not by the BFF gateway. The current decision requires Space evidence and a non-ZDR run (ZeroDataRetention must be false), so ZDR turns and non-Space contexts cannot use owner actions. Each admission needs owner contract, capability-core binding and health attestation, and a forged-call denial test (model-eligibility.ts header); the decision carries no target-resource grant and the owner re-authorizes the target. No cross-plane DB access. Writes need exact-effect approval.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Replace "the BFF gateway mints a per-run scoped delegated token" with generalising Control run-action-v1 and model-action-view-v1 from the single tickets.create case into a per-action table keyed by the catalog schema hash; the BFF keeps minting only per-audience user bearers. Add a model-access class (none, read, write-with-approval) and an exempt reason to ActionDescriptor (risk already exists) and turn the catalog-manifest allowlist test into the CI ratchet. The item restates plan milestones M2 and M3, so reference the plan rather than redefine them.
verevon.effortNote: M holds for the framework tranche (classification fields, CI ratchet, generalising the Control decision table, first read actions). Each further admission is its own M of owner-plane work.
verevon.verdictReason: Risk metadata and per-run scoped authority already exist in part, and the token should be minted by Control rather than the BFF; reword to generalising the existing Control decision, adding model-access classes and the CI ratchet.

title: Human takeover and hand-back from live views: agent-requested takeover for logins, 2FA and CAPTCHAs, then point-and-comment steering
summary: Add a request_human_takeover action that pauses the browser run, switches the hosted browser to human control with a takeover card in chat, and resumes on hand-back with the user's note and a fresh snapshot; human-typed input never flows to the model or into replays. Second track: point-and-comment on live previews and artifacts so the user can steer by clicking an element or drawing a region.
whyItMatters: Logins, 2FA and CAPTCHAs end most real browser tasks; five of twelve references hand control to the human and back (Manus, T3 Code input arbitration). Manual takeover already exists in the hosted browser, so the missing piece is the Model Plane pause and the chat surface.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Manus (agent-suggested takeover cards, hand-back message) plus T3 Code (real human-vs-agent input arbitration by recording expected synthetic input and treating anything else as human) ; Manus (DOC strings: choose a computer, view, take over, pause, exit takeover; a login done during takeover can carry over to similar tasks) for takeover, and Cursor (SRC: design mode in the in-app browser to click elements or draw a region and comment; pausable VNC view; steer from phone) for point-and-comment
others: Manus web (select region plus instruction across builder, slides and design)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-06-02: 5 of 12 sources (common) | R-t3-12-11: 2 of 12 sources for each track (differentiators).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: The agent emits suggest_takeover{surface, reason}; Live view stream (VNC or CDP screencast) in a pane with a takeover state machine {agent_driving, user_driving, paused};

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: R-t3-06-02: Manual takeover works in the hosted browser: controlMode human_takeover blocks model actions in the BFF. | R-t3-12-11: The Work panel shows a live agent screen, but chat turns cannot yet drive a browser, agent browser runs fail closed without a broker grant (DOC), and live view plus takeover is planned as E10 (L to XL) with E9 (Open in browser from a message) as its predecessor;

approachOriginal: Plan E9/E10 plus the durable pause of F-t3-002; T3-style arbitration (record expected synthetic input, treat anything else as human). Point-and-comment reuses the typed annotation part of F-t3-031.
planeOwner: Model Plane (pause and resume) with Ingestion Plane (Quarry control mode) and Frontend Plane (takeover card, live view)
risks: Credentials typed by the human must never reach the model or recordings; a scoped carry-over grant for repeated logins needs an expiry.

title: Deep research v2: clarifying questions and an editable plan, mid-run steering, a gap-driven second pass with a claim ledger, and knowledge plus connector sources in one cited report
summary: Split run_deep_research into a plan phase (sub-queries, optional domain scope, one to three clarifying questions, approve or auto-start) and a run phase that streams interim findings and accepts refocus. Then add a second pass: extract a claim-to-source ledger from pages actually read, issue targeted follow-up queries for gaps and conflicts, stop when new sources add little, and include Data Plane v2 and connector sources so one report cites web, knowledge and apps.
whyItMatters: Verevon already ships honest one-pass research (mandatory 'could not verify' section, cited artifact). Plan transparency (ChatGPT) and gap-driven passes (Codex method, Perplexity scale) are what make research reports trustworthy at depth. Reference evidence here is documentation-only.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: ChatGPT deep research (web-chatgpt, DOC) ; Codex deep-research skill (codexagent-plugins-and-extensibility-097, DOC) for method; Perplexity (web-perplexity-web-product-034, DOC) for scale
others: Perplexity advanced research (web-perplexity, DOC): interim key findings and a streamed editable report
Claude research (claude-product-ux-075, SRC): explicit 'research plan created' state
Manus start card (SRC): an 'Always auto-start' opt-out, a pattern to reuse for plan approval
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-03-01: 3 of 11 sources; differentiator | R-t3-03-02: 5 of 11 sources; common (reference evidence is DOC-only)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Run state machine: clarify (optional, only when the query is broad) -> plan_proposed (structured sub-questions plus allowed or prioritised domains) -> user edits or accepts -> running, emitting source-reading and finding events -> a follow-up or changed site list injected mid-run re-plans the remaining steps -> report streamed incrementally. Loop: plan sub-questions -> pass 1 broad search and read -> extract claims into a claim-to-source ledger -> identify gaps and conflicts -> pass 2 targeted queries -> stop when new sources add little (diminishing-returns test) or the budget is hit -> synthesise from the ledger only, labelling inference -> render and check the artifact.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: R-t3-03-01: SRC: the plan is shown as one checklist row per sub-query and the Kilder tab fills before synthesis, but the run starts immediately. | R-t3-03-02: SRC: one pass (plan up to 9 sub-queries, concurrent search, read of 16 pages, one synthesis with [n] citations, mandatory 'Kunne ikke verifiseres' section, document artifact, wall clock bound).

approachOriginal: Refactor deep_research.rs into plan/run first, reuse plan_proposed and queued_input semantics; then the ledger and pass 2 with per-pass caps; longer evidence windows via the chunked reader of F-t3-054.
risks: Cost of extra passes (synthesis input dominates); client-edited plans are untrusted and must be re-clamped; ZDR blocks persisting the ledger; deep research is rejected on the subscription route.

verevon.exactGap: run_deep_research (deep_research.rs:2413) is one in-stream, web-only pass: plan up to 9 sub-queries (already shown as a per-sub-query checklist before any search), concurrent search, read about 16 pages, citations emitted before synthesis so the Kilder tab fills early, one synthesis with a mandatory could-not-verify section; user-pasted URLs also seed the source list. There is no clarification step, no plan approve or edit (plan_proposed and queued_input serve only the agentic tool loop), no claim ledger or second pass, and no knowledge or connector source: the file has no knowledge or connector code and sse.rs:953 rejects knowledge_only scope together with deep research. Deep research is also refused under ZDR.
reuse: deep_research.rs coverage, read_order, number_and_bound and coverage_statement honesty machinery (keep the mandatory unverified section)
ResearchEvents::Live sink and the existing per-sub-query step rows for plan transparency
plan-approval node and PlanApprovalControl editable step list as UI only
knowledge_search, knowledge_graph_search and knowledge_wiki_search tool definitions in tool_loop.rs (viewer-scoped Data Plane v2 retrieval) for knowledge sources
queued_input registry shape (per request id, tenant and user bound) if steering is kept
linked_source_urls user-seeded sources as the first form of domain scoping
verevon.constraints: The pipeline runs in-process inside one SSE connection with a wall clock and dies with the stream (deep_research.rs header: deliberately not Temporal; queued_input is in-memory single-replica), so an approve-before-run gate cannot wait inside the stream. A research plan approval is not an authority grant: do not reuse PlanProposed rung-grant semantics, only the editable-list UI. Knowledge and connector sources must go through the existing viewer-ACL retrieval path and respect retrieval_scope (auto, knowledge_only, web_only) and Space authority. ZDR and waived-route turns refuse deep research, so the ledger and any plan record are never persisted for them.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Do not refactor one plan/run state machine inside the stream. Ship three independent slices: (1) a plan turn that returns the sub-query list (and at most one clarifying question) as an editable node, then a run turn that carries the edited list and is re-clamped server-side to the 9/10 ceilings; (2) an in-process second pass driven by coverage_of (unread and shortfall are already computed) with one extra search round inside the existing wall clock and page caps, adding a claim ledger only if the synthesis prompt is changed to extract claims (extra inference cost); (3) knowledge and connector sources by calling existing retrieval inside the pipeline under scope rules. Demote mid-run steering: queued_input is delivered only at tool-round boundaries (tool_loop.rs) and deep research is not a tool loop.
verevon.effortNote: Raised from L: the bundle is three separate M to L slices (plan turn, second pass with ledger, knowledge sources) plus steering; as independent items each is M or L.
verevon.verdictReason: The baseline is partly richer than described (plan checklist, early Kilder, user-linked URLs) and the proposed state machine does not fit an in-stream, single-replica pipeline; the item should be split and steering demoted.

title: Canonical reasoning-effort ladder mapped per model to each provider wire format
summary: Define one canonical effort scale (none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh) and a single resolve_effort() in inference-core that every provider adapter calls: clamp the request to the nearest weaker level the model supports, then map it to the provider vocabulary (OpenAI/Azure reasoning effort, Anthropic thinking budget, Codex reasoning_effort, later Gemini thinking level). Start with a static per-model table and move it into the model record (R-t3-09-05) later; keep the composer's Auto / Raskt svar / Dyp research dial as presets over the canonical scale.
whyItMatters: Budget/Balance/Genius defaults are mostly OpenAI-family models, and that route currently sends no reasoning effort at all, so the user's depth choice is ignored on the most-used path. This is a code-verified gap with a small, well-understood fix that six of twelve references implement.

others: codexagent (032, best declared per-model ladder with descriptions)
deepseek (092, refuses unsupported values before dispatch)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: An EFFORT_LADDER plus named per-generation wire vocabularies and clamp_effort() that picks the nearest weaker supported level instead of sending a value that returns 400; capability probes are cached per (model, base_url). The composer renders only the levels the selected model declares. [SRC for Hermes/Codex/DeepSeek]

evidence: grep of inference-core/src/provider/openai.rs finds no reasoning_effort (verified read-only); only codex_subscription.rs sets it

Log the clamp on the run and show the cost multiplier for high levels. Composer reads supported levels from the model record once R-t3-09-05 exists.
risks: Higher effort raises cost and latency; tie default levels to budget posture and show the multiplier. Do not send effort to models that reject the parameter.

title: Content-safety hardening: an injection normaliser, enforcing semantic screening for web and browser content, one policy check on every memory and skill write, and safe links
summary: Add a normaliser before scan_injection (NFKC, strip tag-block and zero-width characters, confusable folding, neutralise forged envelope tags), promote the semantic ContentSafety pass from shadow to enforcing for ExternalWeb and Browser trust classes after a false-positive eval, run one deterministic memory policy (identifiers, account and card numbers, credentials, special-category data) on every memory write path including manual and imported memory, govern skill writes, and add safe-link handling and safety UX.
whyItMatters: Trust-class provenance and a fail-closed scan are already ahead of most references, but the scanner is evadable by Unicode tricks and memory writes outside the extractor bypass the sensitive-data rule. As browser and connector reads arrive (F-t3-008, F-t3-010) injection exposure grows sharply. Perplexity's layered stack and Claude's homoglyph-aware scrubber are the references.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Perplexity (most layered documented stack: intent anchoring, screening classifier, containment, runtime monitoring) and Claude (homoglyph-aware scrubber neutralising forged envelope tags) for injection; Hermes for memory and skill write governance (staged entry-pinned writes, review fork limited to an allowlist, install-scan trust matrix) ; claude (import flow); web-claudeai (sensitive policy); hermes (write-tool mechanics)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-11-07: injection defences 8 of 12 (table-stakes); skill supply chain 5 of 12; moderation UX 4 of 12; memory write governance 2 of 12 | R-t3-08-06: Import: 5 of 12 (common). referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Normalise untrusted text (NFKC, strip U+E0000 tag block and zero-width, neutralise lookalike '<' plus reserved tag names), wrap in a trust-class envelope, tiered pattern scan (strict for context files and memory, advisory for tool results), semantic classifier on external content. Claude shows a fixed export prompt for the other tool, the user pastes the answer, a model call splits it into candidate entries tagged source=import that go through the normal grounding and dedup path and are shown for review before commit.

title: Trajectory ledger with exact model-visible request capture and timing waterfall
summary: Add a complete second view of every run next to the chat: a virtualised, grouped ledger (turn, step, request, tool call, sub-call) with a per-record inspector (raw record, payload, result, tool schema, request options, system prompt in effect, usage, timing) and an Inspect action on each chat tool card. Back it with request_snapshot events written at the model call site (parameters, adapter defaults, content-addressed system-prompt and tool-catalogue blobs, auxiliary calls labelled by purpose) and step-level timing events drawn as a waterfall that shows 'unavailable' instead of estimates.
whyItMatters: DeepSeek's 'maximum information, very transparent' is an explicit Verevon reference, and long Do-mode and browser runs cannot be explained from a flat event list. This is the strongest single transparency gap: users, support and engineers cannot see what the model was actually sent, which also blocks replay tests (R-t3-10-11) and trustworthy audit.

referenceBestPractice.mechanism: DeepSeek keeps the invariant 'model-visible implies logged': one append-only per-session log; a request header event {config, adapterDefaults, tools} is appended only when it differs from the previous one; the system prompt is a diffable event; auxiliary requests are logged before dispatch. The ledger is a projection grouped by turn, step and request with request numbers and cumulative usage, 13 inspector tabs, and an Inspect action on each chat tool card. The waterfall is drawn from recorded timestamps only, with time-to-first-token split from decoding and in-flight records showing only a start marker.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: The Trace tab is a flat durable run-event list capped at 5,000 with proof and receipts. There is no turn/step/request grouping, no inspector tabs, no Inspect link from a tool card. The context inspector (GET /v1/threads/:id/context, GetContextAssembly) shows assembled segments and token counts, but no per-request snapshot of effective parameters, the exact system prompt or the tool catalogue is persisted or served, and auxiliary calls (title, follow-ups, verification pass) are not shown as requests. Timing is per turn (turn_timing phases plus provider intervals), not per step or tool; no copyable trace/request id was found in the chat UI (INF from grep).

approachOriginal: Deliver in three slices. (1) Projection and UI: session-core exposes GET /v1/runs/:id/trajectory that groups stored events by turn, step and request (browser actions grouped by action_id); verevonv3 upgrades the Trace tab to a virtualised grouped ledger with an inspector drawer, and tool-presentation carries the event id so tool cards get Inspect. (2) Request capture: at the model-gateway/execution-core call site write request_snapshot events to session-core (provider, model, effort, params, adapter default flags, tool schema list) only when changed, with system prompt and tool catalogue stored as hash-addressed blobs in MinIO (deduplicated), and purpose-labelled auxiliary calls; under ZDR persist only hashes and parameter metadata and render 'not retained (ZDR)'. Decide which Verevon persona/policy prompt text is shown versus hashed. (3) Timing: emit step_timing {step_id, queued_at, started_at, first_token_at, ended_at} from the existing OTEL spans (including approval wait and hooks), expose trace id on usage, draw the waterfall strip, add a copy-trace-id action. Owner-only access as today; never widen Space ACLs.
planeOwner: Model Plane (session-core, model-gateway, execution-core) and Frontend Plane (Trace tab)
risks: Prompt and payload tabs can expose tenant secrets or other users' content in shared Spaces, so they stay owner-only with redaction and no ACL widening; ZDR must propagate (no prompt content persisted); persona/policy prompt IP visibility needs a decision; storage growth and virtualisation for very large runs; clock skew across services must never be papered over by synthesised timings.
